title: SpaceX Tesla Merger Talks Weigh $3.5 Trillion Combination
summary: Tesla and SpaceX named five directors to negotiate a potential $3.5 trillion all-stock merger, the FT reported, with talks aiming at a year-end deadline.
body_markdown:
Term Reported detail


Size Potential $3.5 trillion combination


Structure Expected all-stock transaction, exchange ratio under negotiation


Negotiators Three Tesla directors, two SpaceX directors


Advisers Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs (SpaceX), Evercore (Tesla)


Timing Moving toward a potential year-end deadline


Tesla shareholder vote More than 50% of all possible votes


## When Could Tesla and SpaceX Announce a Deal?


No date has been set, and people involved cautioned that the committees were not yet close to reaching an agreement, Investing.com reported, citing the FT. Earlier[reports of a SpaceX merger](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/tesla-tsla-stock-news-november-24-2026/) pointed to a similar timeline, with Bloomberg reporting earlier this month that a deal could be announced as early as December, according to Reuters.


[24/7 Wall St.](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/tesla-spacex-could-announce-merger-130802489.html) noted on Nov 13 that a slip into early 2027 had also been discussed, and that Tesla's annual meeting is set for Dec 3, 2026. On SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call last month, Musk said a merger bringing his AI, robotics, EV and aerospace ambitions under one corporate roof would be "a good idea", according to Reuters. On the same call he said the special committees "have not reached agreement on the terms of any transaction, and obviously there's no guarantee that they will," per 24/7 Wall St.


## What the Deal Means for TSLA Shareholders


Tesla shareholders would get a vote. Tesla is expected to need a separate extraordinary shareholder meeting, where the deal must win more than 50% of all possible votes, with abstentions and uncast votes counting against approval, Investing.com reported, citing the FT.


Under the structure reported earlier this month, Tesla holders would receive SpaceX shares, with the number still being negotiated, 24/7 Wall St. reported. Musk controls about 84% of voting rights at SpaceX but around 20% at Tesla, so the merger could significantly reshape his control of the combined company, according to Investing.com.


## Could US and China Regulators Complicate the Deal?


They could. The deal may face regulatory scrutiny in the United States, China, Europe and the United Kingdom, and Tesla's Chinese operations and SpaceX's rocket technology and Starlink satellite business could complicate approvals over national security and geopolitical concerns, Investing.com reported, citing the FT. Reuters likewise described steep regulatory hurdles over SpaceX's US defense contracts and Tesla's reliance on China.
